contentBlocks.text: Last week you mastered linear equations and functions. This week: the Pythagorean theorem, one of math's most famous relationships!

In any right triangle (a triangle with one 90-degree angle), the Pythagorean theorem states: a² + b² = c², where a and b are the two shorter sides (legs) and c is the longest side (hypotenuse, opposite the right angle). This relationship holds true for every single right triangle, no matter the size. Identify the legs and hypotenuse in a right triangle with sides 3, 4, and 5.
You just learned the Pythagorean theorem and identified a triangle's legs and hypotenuse! Tomorrow we'll use it to find a missing hypotenuse.

objectives: State the Pythagorean theorem: a² + b² = c² for right triangles
Correctly identify the legs and hypotenuse of a 3-4-5 right triangle
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's linear-equations work briefly.
2. Introduce the Pythagorean theorem and right-triangle vocabulary (legs, hypotenuse).
3. Have the child identify the parts of a 3-4-5 triangle.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's finding-the-hypotenuse lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: draw an actual right triangle and label the right angle first, to make identifying the hypotenuse (opposite it) concrete
Ready for more: ask the child to verify that 3² + 4² actually equals 5² using real arithmetic
Opens this week's Pythagorean-theorem thread from the course's own description, using the classic 3-4-5 triangle
teacherGuide.answerKey: The legs are 3 and 4; the hypotenuse (opposite the right angle, the longest side) is 5.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 8 standard 8.G.6: explaining a proof of the Pythagorean theorem, opening this week's thread from the course's own description.
